statement: CoreWeave reports first measured performance for Vera Rubin, claiming 10x more tokens per megawatt than Blackwell.
why: If a generation shift multiplies tokens per megawatt, buyers with fixed power allocations get far more sellable output per site, which raises the value of upgrading rather than adding power.

impact.mechanism: More tokens per megawatt lifts revenue per constrained megawatt, strengthening the case to buy Rubin racks and easing the power ceiling on inference capacity growth.

evidence.excerpt: 10x more tokens per megawatt than Blackwell

confidence.basis: Self-reported vendor benchmark on a company blog, with no test conditions, workload or interactivity target disclosed in the document.

dispersion: Conditions, workload and comparison configuration for the 10x figure are not stated in the article.
